biography.plain_text: Albert Obrist is a Swiss packaging entrepreneur whose team developed and commercialised screw closures for beverage bottles. After selling his first company, he continued manufacturing tubes for food and medicines in Reinach, near Basel. His industrial career also financed a longstanding interest in collecting Ferraris and restoring historic cars and sailing craft.

long_biography.plain_text:
For Albert Obrist, restoring a Ferrari meant preserving its original engineering, even when modern components would improve its performance. The Swiss industrialist assembled cars spanning the marque's development, working with specialist mechanics in Maranello. He regarded the undertaking as a cultural project, building lasting relationships with drivers and craftsmen rather than treating the cars simply as investments.

That concern for authenticity also shaped Fairlie Restorations, which he established in 1987. Its work drew on an archive of more than 1,200 Fife documents. Obrist insisted on agreeing a restoration plan before work began and preserving original material wherever possible. Reconstructing interiors required particular care: surviving drawings often recorded hulls but left much of the original cabinetmakers' work undocumented.
